sanskrit: vasiṣṭhas tu tadā rāmam uktvā rājapurohitaḥ abravīd dharmasaṃyuktaṃ punar evāparaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then Vasiṣṭha, the royal chaplain, having spoken to Rāma, spoke again further words joined with righteousness.

sanskrit: puruṣasyeha jātasya bhavanti guravas trayaḥ ācāryaś caiva kākutstha pitā mātā ca rāghava
english: For a man born into this world there are three teachers, O Kākutstha — the preceptor, the father, and the mother, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: pitā hy enaṃ janayati puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha prajñāṃ dadāti cācāryas tasmāt sa gurur ucyate
english: The father begets a man, O bull among men, while the preceptor bestows wisdom — therefore he is called a guru.

sanskrit: sa te 'haṃ pitur ācāryas tava caiva paraṃtapa mama tvaṃ vacanaṃ kurvan nātivarteḥ satāṃ gatim
english: I am your father's preceptor and yours as well, O scorcher of foes; by acting on my words you shall not transgress the path of the righteous.

sanskrit: imā hi te pariṣadaḥ śreṇayaś ca samāgatāḥ eṣu tāta caran dharmaṃ nātivarteḥ satāṃ gatim
english: These assemblies and guilds are gathered here before you; by practicing righteousness among them, dear child, you shall not transgress the path of the good.

sanskrit: vṛddhāyā dharmaśīlāyā mātur nārhasy avartitum asyās tu vacanaṃ kurvan nātivarteḥ satāṃ gatim
english: You ought not to disobey your aged and virtuous mother; by acting on her word you shall not transgress the path of the righteous.

sanskrit: bharatasya vacaḥ kurvan yācamānasya rāghava ātmānaṃ nātivartes tvaṃ satyadharmaparākrama
english: By acting on the words of Bharata who beseeches you, O Rāghava, you shall not transgress yourself, O you of valor in truth and righteousness.

sanskrit: evaṃ madhuram uktas tu guruṇā rāghavaḥ svayam pratyuvāca samāsīnaṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ
english: Thus sweetly addressed by his guru, Rāghava himself, that bull among men, replied to Vasiṣṭha who was seated before him.

sanskrit: yan mātāpitarau vṛttaṃ tanaye kurutaḥ sadā na supratikaraṃ tat tu mātrā pitrā ca yat kṛtam
english: What mother and father constantly do for a child — what has been done by mother and by father — that is not easily requited.

sanskrit: yathāśakti pradānena snāpanāc chādanena ca nityaṃ ca priyavādena tathā saṃvardhanena ca
english: By giving according to their ability, by bathing and clothing, by constant affectionate speech, and by fostering growth —

sanskrit: sa hi rājā janayitā pitā daśaratho mama ājñātaṃ yan mayā tasya na tan mithyā bhaviṣyati
english: For king Daśaratha who begot me is my father; what I have been commanded by him shall not prove false.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa bharataḥ pratyanantaram uvāca paramodāraḥ sūtaṃ paramadurmanāḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Bharata, most noble but deeply distressed, immediately spoke to the charioteer.

sanskrit: iha me sthaṇḍile śīghraṃ kuśān āstara sārathe āryaṃ pratyupavekṣyāmi yāvan me na prasīdati
english: "Spread kuśa grass for me quickly on this bare ground, charioteer — I shall lie down here facing my elder brother until he relents toward me."

sanskrit: anāhāro nirāloko dhanahīno yathā dvijaḥ śeṣye purastāc chālāyā yāvan na pratiyāsyati
english: "Without food, without seeking shelter, without wealth, like a twice-born ascetic, I shall lie before this hermitage until he returns."

sanskrit: sa tu rāmam avekṣantaṃ sumantraṃ prekṣya durmanāḥ kuśottaram upasthāpya bhūmāv evāstarat svayam
english: Sorrowful, seeing Sumatra looking toward Rāma, he had the kuśa grass spread and himself laid it out on the ground.

sanskrit: tam uvāca mahātejā rāmo rājarṣisattamāḥ kiṃ māṃ bharata kurvāṇaṃ tāta pratyupavekṣyasi
english: Then Rāma of great splendor, the foremost of royal sages, spoke to him: "Why, dear Bharata, do you lie down here facing me in this manner?"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo hy ekapārśvena narān roddhum ihārhati na tu mūrdhāvasiktānāṃ vidhiḥ pratyupaveśane
english: "A brahmin may lie on one side to press men by this rite, but the practice of lying prostrate before the consecrated is not proper for them."

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha naraśārdūla hitvaitad dāruṇaṃ vratam puravaryām itaḥ kṣipram ayodhyāṃ yāhi rāghava
english: "Rise, O tiger among men; abandon this harsh vow; return hence quickly to Ayodhyā, foremost of cities, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: āsīnas tv eva bharataḥ paurajānapadaṃ janam uvāca sarvataḥ prekṣya kim āryaṃ nānuśāsatha
english: But Bharata, remaining seated, looked all around at the townspeople and country folk and said: "Why do you not instruct my elder brother?"

sanskrit: te tam ūcur mahātmānaṃ paurajānapadā janāḥ kākutstham abhijānīmaḥ samyag vadati rāghavaḥ
english: The townspeople and country folk said to that great-souled one: "We acknowledge the Kākutstha speaks rightly and well."

sanskrit: eṣo 'pi hi mahābhāgaḥ pitur vacasi tiṣṭhati ata eva na śaktāḥ smo vyāvartayitum añjasā
english: "This illustrious one himself abides in his father's word; therefore we are not able to turn him away from it forthwith."

sanskrit: teṣām ājñāya vacanaṃ rāmo vacanam abravīt evaṃ nibodha vacanaṃ suhṛdāṃ dharmacakṣuṣām
english: Understanding the words of those people, Rāma spoke: "Hear thus the counsel of friends who see through the eye of righteousness."

sanskrit: etac caivobhayaṃ śrutvā samyak saṃpaśya rāghava uttiṣṭha tvaṃ mahābāho māṃ ca spṛśa tathodakam
english: "Having heard both these things and considered rightly, O Rāghava, rise, O mighty-armed one, and touch water with me."

sanskrit: athotthāya jalaṃ spṛṣṭvā bharato vākyam abravīt śṛṇvantu me pariṣado mantriṇaḥ śreṇayas tathā
english: Then, having risen and touched water, Bharata spoke these words: "Let the assemblies, ministers, and guilds listen to me."

sanskrit: na yāce pitaraṃ rājyaṃ nānuśāsāmi mātaram āryaṃ paramadharmajñam abhijānāmi rāghavam
english: "I did not beg my father for the kingdom, nor do I instruct my mother; I acknowledge my elder brother Rāghava as supremely versed in righteousness."

sanskrit: yadi tv avaśyaṃ vastavyaṃ kartavyaṃ ca pitur vacaḥ aham eva nivatsyāmi caturdaśa vane samāḥ
english: "But if the forest must indeed be dwelt in and the father's command must be fulfilled, then I myself will live in the forest for fourteen years."

sanskrit: dharmātmā tasya tathyena bhrātur vākyena vismitaḥ uvāca rāmaḥ saṃprekṣya paurajānapadaṃ janam
english: The righteous-souled Rāma, astonished by his brother's truthful speech, looked at the townspeople and country folk and spoke.

sanskrit: vikrītam āhitaṃ krītaṃ yat pitrā jīvatā mama na tal lopayituṃ śakyaṃ mayā vā bharatena vā
english: "What was pledged, what was entrusted, what was granted by my father while he lived — neither I nor Bharata is able to annul that."

sanskrit: upadhir na mayā kāryo vanavāse jugupsitaḥ yuktam uktaṃ ca kaikeyyā pitrā me sukṛtaṃ kṛtam
english: "I should not resort to deceit in my forest dwelling, which would be contemptible; what was said by Kaikeyī was fitting, and my father did what was well done."

sanskrit: jānāmi bharataṃ kṣāntaṃ gurusatkārakāriṇam sarvam evātra kalyāṇaṃ satyasaṃdhe mahātmani
english: "I know Bharata to be forbearing and devoted to the honor of his elders; all good resides in this great-souled one who is steadfast in truth."

sanskrit: anena dharmaśīlena vanāt pratyāgataḥ punaḥ bhrātrā saha bhaviṣyāmi pṛthivyāḥ patir uttamaḥ
english: "Returned from the forest, I shall be the supreme lord of the earth together with this dharma-natured brother."

sanskrit: vṛto rājā hi kaikeyyā mayā tad vacanaṃ kṛtam anṛtān mocayānena pitaraṃ taṃ mahīpatim
english: "The king was implored by Kaikeyī; I have fulfilled that command — by this I shall free that lord of the earth, my father, from untruth."

sanskrit: tam apratimatejobhyāṃ bhrātṛbhyāṃ romaharṣaṇam vismitāḥ saṃgamaṃ prekṣya samavetā maharṣayaḥ
english: The great sages assembled there, struck with wonder, watched the hair-raising meeting of those two brothers of incomparable splendor.

sanskrit: antarhitās tv ṛṣigaṇāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ tau bhrātarau mahātmānau kākutsthau praśaśaṃsire
english: The invisible hosts of sages and perfected beings, supreme seers, praised those two great-souled Kākutstha brothers.

sanskrit: sa dhanyo yasya putrau dvau dharmajñau dharmavikramau śrutvā vayaṃ hi saṃbhāṣām ubhayoḥ spṛhayāmahe
english: "Blessed is he whose two sons are both learned in righteousness and heroic in virtue; having heard the exchange of both, we are filled with longing."

sanskrit: tatas tv ṛṣigaṇāḥ kṣipraṃ daśagrīvavadhaiṣiṇaḥ bharataṃ rājaśārdūlam ity ūcuḥ saṃgatā vacaḥ
english: Then the assembled sages who desired the slaying of Daśagrīva quickly spoke these words to Bharata, that tiger among kings.

sanskrit: kule jāta mahāprājña mahāvṛtta mahāyaśaḥ grāhyaṃ rāmasya vākyaṃ te pitaraṃ yady avekṣase
english: "Born of a noble lineage, O greatly wise one, of great conduct and great fame — you should accept Rāma's word, if you regard your father."

sanskrit: sadānṛṇam imaṃ rāmaṃ vayam icchāmahe pituḥ anṛṇatvāc ca kaikeyyāḥ svargaṃ daśaratho gataḥ
english: "We wish this Rāma to be forever free of debt to his father; and through freedom from debt to Kaikeyī, Daśaratha has gone to heaven."

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ gandharvāḥ samaharṣayaḥ rājarṣayaś caiva tathā sarve svāṃ svāṃ gatiṃ gatāḥ
english: Having spoken these words, the gandharvas together with the sages and all the royal sages departed each to his own destination.

sanskrit: hlāditas tena vākyena śubhena śubhadarśanaḥ rāmaḥ saṃhṛṣṭavadanas tān ṛṣīn abhyapūjayat
english: Gladdened by those auspicious words, Rāma of auspicious aspect, his face lit with joy, paid honor to those sages.

sanskrit: srastagātras tu bharataḥ sa vācā sajjamānayā kṛtāñjalir idaṃ vākyaṃ rāghavaṃ punar abravīt
english: But Bharata, his body slack, his voice faltering, with palms joined, spoke again these words to Rāghava.

sanskrit: rājadharmam anuprekṣya kuladharmānusaṃtatim kartum arhasi kākutstha mama mātuś ca yācanām
english: "Considering the duty of a king and the succession of the family's dharma, you ought to fulfill the entreaty of me and of my mother, O Kākutstha."

sanskrit: rakṣituṃ sumahad rājyaṃ aham ekas tu notsahe paurajānapadāṃś cāpi raktān rañjayituṃ tathā
english: "I alone do not venture to protect this vast kingdom, nor to delight the townspeople and countryfolk who are devoted to you."

sanskrit: jñātayaś ca hi yodhāś ca mitrāṇi suhṛdaś ca naḥ tvām eva pratikāṅkṣante parjanyam iva karṣakāḥ
english: "Our kinsmen, warriors, allies, and friends await you alone, as farmers await the rain cloud."

sanskrit: idaṃ rājyaṃ mahāprājña sthāpaya pratipadya hi śaktimān asi kākutstha lokasya paripālane
english: "Accept and establish this kingdom, O greatly wise one; you are capable, O Kākutstha, of protecting the world."

sanskrit: ity uktvā nyapatad bhrātuḥ pādayor bharatas tadā bhṛśaṃ saṃprārthayām āsa rāmam evaṃ priyaṃ vadaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, Bharata fell then at his brother's feet, earnestly entreating Rāma with these affectionate words.

sanskrit: tam aṅke bhrātaraṃ kṛtvā rāmo vacanam abravīt śyāmaṃ nalinapatrākṣaṃ mattahaṃsasvaraḥ svayam
english: Taking his brother upon his lap, Rāma himself spoke, dark-complexioned, lotus-petal-eyed, his voice like that of a lordly swan.

sanskrit: āgatā tvām iyaṃ buddhiḥ svajā vainayikī ca yā bhṛśam utsahase tāta rakṣituṃ pṛthivīm api
english: "This resolve that has come to you is your own and born of proper training, by which you venture so greatly, dear one, to protect the earth."

sanskrit: amātyaiś ca suhṛdbhiś ca buddhimadbhiś ca mantribhiḥ sarvakāryāṇi saṃmantrya sumahānty api kāraya
english: "Together with ministers, friends, and wise counselors, deliberating on all matters, have even the greatest affairs carried out."

sanskrit: lakṣmīś candrād apeyād vā himavān vā himaṃ tyajet atīyāt sāgaro velāṃ na pratijñām ahaṃ pituḥ
english: "Lakṣmī might depart from the moon, or the Himālaya might give up its snow, or the ocean might overflow its shore — I shall not break my father's vow."

sanskrit: kāmād vā tāta lobhād vā mātrā tubhyam idaṃ kṛtam na tan manasi kartavyaṃ vartitavyaṃ ca mātṛvat
english: "Whether done out of desire or greed by your mother for your sake, dear one, you should not take that to heart; treat her as a mother."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ bharataḥ kausalyāsutam abravīt tejasādityasaṃkāśaṃ pratipaccandradarśanam
english: As he spoke thus, Bharata addressed the son of Kausalyā, who was resplendent as the sun, whose appearance was like the crescent moon.

sanskrit: adhirohārya pādābhyāṃ pāduke hemabhūṣite ete hi sarvalokasya yogakṣemaṃ vidhāsyataḥ
english: "Have these golden-adorned sandals mounted upon your feet; these will ensure the welfare and security of all the world."

sanskrit: so 'dhiruhya naravyāghraḥ pāduke hy avaruhya ca prāyacchat sumahātejā bharatāya mahātmane
english: Then that tiger among men of very great splendor mounted the sandals and then dismounted them, and presented them to the great-souled Bharata.

sanskrit: sa pāduke te bharataḥ pratāpavān svalaṃkṛte saṃparigṛhya dharmavit pradakṣiṇaṃ caiva cakāra rāghavaṃ cakāra caivottamanāgamūrdhani
english: The valorous Bharata, knower of dharma, reverently received those well-adorned sandals, circumambulated Rāghava, and then placed them on the head of the finest elephant.

sanskrit: athānupūrvyāt pratipūjya taṃ janaṃ gurūṃś ca mantriprakṛtīs tathānujau vyasarjayad rāghavavaṃśavardhanaḥ sthitaḥ svadharme himavān ivācalaḥ
english: Then, having honored in due order the people, the elders, ministers and nobles, and his two younger brothers, he who advances the Rāghava lineage dismissed them, himself standing firm in his own dharma, immovable as the Himālaya.

sanskrit: taṃ mātaro bāṣpagṛhītakaṇṭho duḥkhena nāmantrayituṃ hi śekuḥ sa tv eva mātṝr abhivādya sarvā rudan kuṭīṃ svāṃ praviveśa rāmaḥ
english: His mothers, their throats choked with tears, could not address him out of grief; but he, having saluted all the mothers, weeping, entered his own hut.

sanskrit: tataḥ śirasi kṛtvā tu pāduke bharatas tadā āruroha rathaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ śatrughnena samanvitaḥ
english: Then Bharata, having placed the sandals upon his head, joyfully mounted his chariot accompanied by Śatrughna.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭho vāmadevaś ca jābāliś ca dṛḍhavrataḥ agrataḥ prayayuḥ sarve mantriṇo mantrapūjitāḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha, Vāmadeva, and Jābāli of firm vows went ahead, all the ministers honored with sacred formulas.

sanskrit: mandākinīṃ nadīṃ ramyāṃ prāṅmukhās te yayus tadā pradakṣiṇaṃ ca kurvāṇāś citrakūṭaṃ mahāgirim
english: Facing eastward, they went along the lovely river Mandākinī, circumambulating the great mountain Citrakūṭa.

sanskrit: paśyan dhātusahasrāṇi ramyāṇi vividhāni ca prayayau tasya pārśvena sasainyo bharatas tadā
english: Beholding thousands of beautiful and various minerals and ores, Bharata then proceeded along its flanks with his army.

sanskrit: adūrāc citrakūṭasya dadarśa bharatas tadā āśramaṃ yatra sa munir bharadvājaḥ kṛtālayaḥ
english: Not far from Citrakūṭa, Bharata then saw the hermitage where the sage Bharadvāja had made his dwelling.

sanskrit: sa tam āśramam āgamya bharadvājasya buddhimān avatīrya rathāt pādau vavande kulanandanaḥ
english: That wise delight of his lineage, having reached Bharadvāja's hermitage, descended from his chariot and venerated his feet.

sanskrit: tato hṛṣṭo bharadvājo bharataṃ vākyam abravīt api kṛtyaṃ kṛtaṃ tāta rāmeṇa ca samāgatam
english: Then Bharadvāja, pleased, spoke to Bharata: "Has the purpose been accomplished, dear child — have you met with Rāma?"

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bharato bharadvājena dhīmatā pratyuvāca bharadvājaṃ bharato dharmavatsalaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the wise Bharadvāja, Bharata, who cherished righteousness, replied to Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: sa yācyamāno guruṇā mayā ca dṛḍhavikramaḥ rāghavaḥ paramaprīto vasiṣṭhaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: "He of firm valor, Rāghava, when entreated by the guru and by me, being greatly pleased, spoke these words to Vasiṣṭha:"

sanskrit: pituḥ pratijñāṃ tām eva pālayiṣyāmi tattvataḥ caturdaśa hi varṣāṇi ya pratijñā pitur mama
english: "'I shall truly uphold that very vow of my father — the vow my father made — for fourteen years.'"

sanskrit: evam ukto mahāprājño vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha vākyajño vākyakuśalaṃ rāghavaṃ vacanaṃ mahat
english: Thus addressed, the greatly wise Vasiṣṭha, versed in speech, replied with a great utterance to the speech-skilled Rāghava.

sanskrit: ete prayaccha saṃhṛṣṭaḥ pāduke hemabhūṣite ayodhyāyāṃ mahāprājña yogakṣemakare tava
english: "'Present with joy these golden-adorned sandals, O greatly wise one; they shall ensure your welfare and security in Ayodhyā.'"

sanskrit: evam ukto vasiṣṭhena rāghavaḥ prāṅmukhaḥ sthitaḥ pāduke hemavikṛte mama rājyāya te dadau
english: "Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, Rāghava stood facing east and gave those golden sandals to me for my kingdom."

sanskrit: nivṛtto 'ham anujñāto rāmeṇa sumahātmanā ayodhyām eva gacchāmi gṛhītvā pāduke śubhe
english: "'I have turned back, having been permitted by Rāma of very great soul; I go to Ayodhyā itself, bearing these auspicious sandals.'"

sanskrit: etac chrutvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ bharatasya mahātmanaḥ bharadvājaḥ śubhataraṃ munir vākyam udāharat
english: Having heard this auspicious speech of the great-souled Bharata, the sage Bharadvāja pronounced a still more auspicious speech.

sanskrit: naitac citraṃ naravyāghra śīlavṛttavatāṃ vara yad āryaṃ tvayi tiṣṭhet tu nimne vṛṣṭim ivodakam
english: "This is no wonder, O tiger among men, O best of those of noble character and conduct, that nobility should rest in you as water flows to a hollow."

sanskrit: amṛtaḥ sa mahābāhuḥ pitā daśarathas tava yasya tvam īdṛśaḥ putro dharmātmā dharmavatsalaḥ
english: "Immortal is that long-armed father of yours, Daśaratha, whose son you are — such a righteous soul, devoted to dharma."

sanskrit: tam ṛṣiṃ tu mahātmānam uktavākyaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ āmantrayitum ārebhe caraṇāv upagṛhya ca
english: Having been spoken to by that great-souled sage, Bharata with palms joined and clasping his feet began to take leave of him.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā bharadvājaṃ punaḥ punaḥ bharatas tu yayau śrīmān ayodhyāṃ saha mantribhiḥ
english: Then, having circumambulated Bharadvāja again and again, the illustrious Bharata departed for Ayodhyā together with his ministers.

sanskrit: yānaiś ca śakaṭaiś caiva hayaiś nāgaiś ca sā camūḥ punar nivṛttā vistīrṇā bharatasyānuyāyinī
english: That vast army following Bharata, with vehicles, carts, horses, and elephants, turned back once more.

sanskrit: tatas te yamunāṃ divyāṃ nadīṃ tīrtvormimālinīm dadṛśus tāṃ punaḥ sarve gaṅgāṃ śivajalāṃ nadīm
english: Then, having crossed the divine river Yamunā garlanded with waves, they all beheld once again the river Gaṅgā with her auspicious waters.

sanskrit: tāṃ ramyajalasaṃpūrṇāṃ saṃtīrya saha bāndhavaḥ śṛṅgaverapuraṃ ramyaṃ praviveśa sasainikaḥ
english: Having crossed that lovely river full of delightful water, he entered, together with his kinsmen and army, the beautiful town of Śṛṅgaverapura.

sanskrit: śṛṅgaverapurād bhūya ayodhyāṃ saṃdadarśa ha bharato duḥkhasaṃtaptaḥ sārathiṃ cedam abravīt
english: From Śṛṅgaverapura, Bharata then saw Ayodhyā again; scorched with grief, he spoke these words to his charioteer.

sanskrit: sārathe paśya vidhvastā ayodhyā na prakāśate nirākārā nirānandā dīnā pratihatasvanā
english: "Charioteer, see — Ayodhyā is destroyed, it does not shine; it is without beauty, without joy, wretched, its sounds muffled and silent."
